question: does a learned continuous chemical embedding beat the Morgan fingerprint
source: PerturbNet, Yu et al., Mol Syst Biol 21:960-982 (2025)
tokeniser: their smiles_to_hot and pad_smile, loaded verbatim from perturbnet/util.py, char_list=None so their default 35-character list is used
standardisation: (z - mu) / std using their published mu.npy and std.npy
our_step: RDKit canonicalisation and salt stripping (largest covalent fragment). Their smiles_to_hot does not canonicalise. Salt stripping is INFERRED from their Methods phrase about canonical forms, not stated; without it 162 of 188 encode, with it 183, against their reported 180
conclusion: ChemicalVAE loses to the Morgan fingerprint on all three splits and to pathway annotation by a wide margin
